rows.note: Only SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA256 are used (grep: no MD5/SHA1). HMAC test pins key dependence and normalisation.
The CRM stores no passwords; sign-in is Entra ID OIDC code flow with PKCE. Database access is by managed identity. (Local dev SQL password exists only in appsettings.Development.json.)
Integrity uses SHA-256 for documents, billing content digests, privacy manifests and the audit chain; the document hash is verified before download/send (AC03). No SHA-1/MD5.
No keys are derived from passwords anywhere in src (no Rfc2898/PBKDF/Argon use found).

HMAC key is CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM(32); lease owner tokens use Guid.NewGuid (CSPRNG v4 on .NET); OIDC state/nonce/PKCE and cookie keys come from the framework. Random.Shared is only used for retry jitter. Ids are partly time-ordered (SequentialId: 8 random bytes), so authorization must not rely on id secrecy - it does not (record scope returns 404).

Key generation is done by Key Vault (RSA), SQL CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM and the Data Protection framework; the app generates no signatures itself (Entra assertions are signed by MSAL with the Key Vault certificate). Key Vault SKU is standard (software-protected), noted for V13.3.3 (L3).

SQL minimalTlsVersion 1.2 and storage TLS1_2 are set in IaC; no SslProtocols override exists in src so .NET uses OS defaults (1.2/1.3). The public ingress TLS versions are platform-managed by Azure Container Apps and nothing in the repo or smoke.sh verifies the served protocol set (no testssl/ZAP; docs/07 says ZAP is not implemented). || Post-fix reassessment 2026-10-05: still open - No post-deploy TLS version check was added to tools/release/smoke.sh; platform-managed

findings.title: Entra refresh tokens cached unencrypted in SQL (identity.TokenCache)
findings.description: EnableTokenAcquisitionToCallDownstreamApi().AddDistributedTokenCaches() backed by AddDistributedSqlServerCache stores MSAL user token caches (including refresh tokens for Graph delegated mail/calendar) in identity.TokenCache. No MsalDistributedTokenCacheAdapterOptions.Encrypt is configured and, to my knowledge of the library, the default is false, so values are serialized MSAL cache blobs readable by anyone with SELECT (DBA, backup holder, SQL injection). Not executed against a running database.
findings.reproduction: Sign in via Entra, then `SELECT TOP 1 Value FROM identity.TokenCache` as a reader of the identity schema and look for refresh_token entries in the (base64) payload; integration test could assert the stored bytes do not contain the token.
findings.fix: services.Configure<MsalDistributedTokenCacheAdapterOptions>(o => o.Encrypt = true) in AuthenticationSetup (Data Protection is already Key Vault-wrapped), add an integration test, and shorten cache sliding expiry to the 12 h absolute session.

findings.title: Partner Center and Teams webhook secrets have no Key Vault path in infrastructure
findings.description: IaC wires only PowerOffice and Atera secrets from Key Vault. Partner Center ClientSecret/RefreshToken and the Teams webhook URLs (a bearer secret by design, GraphTeams.cs:10-13) are plain configuration; the runbook instructs user-secrets, and in Container Apps the only remaining option is a plain env value visible to anyone who can read the app. Docs (06 §5) say these live in Key Vault, SEC-AUTH-05 says certificates not client secrets, and nothing writes a rotated refresh token back.
findings.reproduction: Enable Integrations__PartnerCenter__Enabled or Teams in prod: apps.bicep has no secretRef for them, so the values can only be supplied as env value:.
findings.fix: Add enablePartnerCenter/enableTeams params, KV-backed secrets in integrationSecrets and workerSecretNames, an architecture test like Provider_secrets_are_resolved_by_crm_worker_only, and certificate credentials for Partner Center.
findings.fixed_by: Key Vault references for Partner Center and Teams secrets in apps.bicep; refresh-token write-back and certificate auth are code changes

findings.title: Forwarded headers trust any sender and host filtering is off
findings.description: KnownProxies/KnownIPNetworks are cleared and XForwardedHost is honoured, with AllowedHosts "*". Anything that can reach port 8080 directly (another app or compromised replica in the environment) can set client IP (audit, rate-limit fallback), scheme and host. The OIDC redirect URI follows the host, which Entra rejects unless registered. I could not determine whether the ACA envoy strips client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host.
findings.reproduction: From a peer container in the environment: `curl -H "X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4" -H "X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example" http://ca-crm-web-prod:8080/bff/login` and inspect the redirect_uri / audit IP.
findings.fix: Set AllowedHosts per environment (FQDN plus the --candidate label host), set KnownIPNetworks to the apps subnet 10.40.0.0/23, drop XForwardedHost unless needed, add a test.

findings.title: HSTS lifetime is the framework default, weaker than documented

findings.fix: services.AddHsts(o => { o.MaxAge = TimeSpan.FromDays(365); o.IncludeSubDomains = true; }) and assert the value in smoke.sh.

findings.title: Privacy HMAC key lives in the same database as the hashes it protects
